# 10tap-editor documentation

> Rich text editor for React Native, built on TipTap and ProseMirror running in a WebView. Typed, works out of the box with a toolbar, and is extended through bridge extensions.

Every page of https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/intro, in sidebar order. Each page starts with its URL.

---

Source: https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/intro

# 10tap-editor

TenTap is a typed, easy to use, customizable, and extendable Rich Text editor for React-Native based on Tiptap and Prosemirror. It offers a "plug and play" experience and comes with many essential features out of the box that can be incorporated into your apps quickly. Additionally, TenTap allows you the developers to tailor the editor to your applications specific needs.

# Features

- 💁 Based on tiptap
- ➕ Extendable
- ⚙️ Support dynamic scheme
- 🛠️ Native toolbar
- 🎹 Custom keyboards
- 💅 Customizable styles
- 🌒 Darkmode and custom theme support
- 🏗️ Supports the new architecture (including bridgeless) and the old architecture

See [Installation](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/setup/installation#requirements) for the supported React Native versions.

## Why?

After years of developing rich text editors for mobile, we realized that there is an empty void for open source RichText editors on mobile especially for ReactNative. So we have decided to create this package that incorporates all that we have learned, and that provides the best possible ux. Tentap is designed for getting the best experience of editing rich-text on mobile inspired by state of the art mobile editors like: gdocs, notion, dropbox paper.

## Installation

```bash
yarn add @10play/tentap-editor react-native-webview
cd ios && pod install
```

With Expo: `npx expo install @10play/tentap-editor react-native-webview`. The editor works in Expo Go; for the native custom keyboard driver use a [development build](https://docs.expo.dev/develop/development-builds/introduction/).

See [Installation](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/setup/installation) for the details and the supported versions. Upgrading from an older version? See the [1.1 migration guide](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/migrations/v1.1).

## Usage

```tsx
import React from 'react';
import { StyleSheet, View } from 'react-native';
import { SafeAreaView } from 'react-native-safe-area-context';
import {
  EditorKeyboardAvoidingView,
  RichText,
  Toolbar,
  useEditorBridge,
} from '@10play/tentap-editor';

export const Basic = () => {
  const editor = useEditorBridge({
    autofocus: true,
    avoidIosKeyboard: true,
    initialContent: 'Start editing!',
  });

  return (
    <SafeAreaView style={styles.fullScreen}>
      <EditorKeyboardAvoidingView style={styles.fullScreen}>
        <View style={styles.fullScreen}>
          <RichText editor={editor} />
        </View>
        <View style={styles.toolbarRow}>
          <Toolbar editor={editor} />
        </View>
      </EditorKeyboardAvoidingView>
    </SafeAreaView>
  );
};

const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  fullScreen: { flex: 1 },
  toolbarRow: { flexDirection: 'row' },
});
```

`EditorKeyboardAvoidingView` keeps the toolbar on top of the keyboard without a `keyboardVerticalOffset`, also on edge-to-edge Android. See [Keyboard and caret](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/setup/keyboard).

## Example apps

The repository has two example apps you can run:

- [`example/`](https://github.com/10play/10tap-editor/tree/main/example): a React Native CLI app (React Native 0.81, new and old architecture) with every example in these docs, including custom keyboards, dynamic height, a navigation header and the [advanced setup](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/setup/advancedSetup).
- [`example-expo/`](https://github.com/10play/10tap-editor/tree/main/example-expo): an Expo app (development build) with the basic editor, dynamic height, custom keyboards in both layouts and two editors on one screen, in light and dark mode. It also runs on the web.

Questions? Check the [FAQ](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/faq).

# Main Concept

`EditorBridge` - a bridge to control the editor from the native side - will be extended by `bridgeExtensions`

`bridgeExtension` - a typed class that helps us communicate between the native part and the webview part

There are two different ways to work with this lib: [simple](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/mainConcepts#simple-usage) and [advanced](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/mainConcepts#advanced-usage), simple should be good enough for most of the cases, we tried to make the API as simple as possible so people will be able to plug and play, on the other hand advanced usage requires a longer setup.

## Simple usage

With the simple usage you get all the standard rich text abilities as you can get from other libs like:

[react-native-pell-rich-editor](https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-native-pell-rich-editor) /
[react-native-cn-quill](https://github.com/imnapo/react-native-cn-quill)

- ordered / bullet / check Lists
- Bold/Italic/Underline
- Placeholder
- Image
- color/highlight
- and more...

With the simple usage you have all of [these](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions) bridgeExtensions available.

With tentap you can also control the scheme of your editor by passing the useBridgeEditor list of bridgeExtensions you want, so in case you build a chat app and you don't want to let users underline you should not pass the Underline bridgeExtension, that will make sure that even if the user will copy paste some text with underline, when pasted the underline will not be parsed.

Custom keyboards - custom keyboards let you swap the system keyboard for a React Native view, for example a color picker or a sticker panel, while the editor keeps its focus, caret and selection. See the [color keyboard example](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/colorKeyboard) and the [custom keyboard example](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/customKeyboard).

## Advanced usage

In case you want to add your own tiptap extension / build your own bridgeExtension you will have to bundle the web editor by your own that way you will get full control of what running inside the webview.

In this case we provide utils/components/hooks that can help you customize the editor but still get all the features and exp fixes tentap can offer.

See the [advanced setup](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/setup/advancedSetup)

You can also see an example in [`example/src/Examples/Advanced`](https://github.com/10play/10tap-editor/tree/main/example/src/Examples/Advanced).

---

Source: https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/faq

# FAQ

### How do I get the content in `onChange`?

`onChange` only tells you that the content changed. It doesn't pass the content, because sending the whole document from the WebView on every keystroke is expensive. Use [useEditorContent](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/useEditorContent), which fetches it for you (debounced, and only when the content changes):

```tsx
const editor = useEditorBridge({ initialContent });
const content = useEditorContent(editor, { type: 'html' }); // or 'text' | 'json'

useEffect(() => {
  if (content !== undefined) save(content);
}, [content]);
```

Or call `await editor.getHTML()` (or `getText` / `getJSON`) inside `onChange`, ideally debounced. See [Working with content](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/workingWithContent).

### Where is `toggleBold`? TypeScript says it doesn't exist on `EditorBridge`.

`toggleBold` and the other formatting commands are added to `EditorBridge` by their bridge extensions. `toggleBold` comes from `BoldBridge`, which is part of the default `TenTapStartKit`. If you pass your own `bridgeExtensions`, include the bridges whose commands you use. All the commands are listed on [EditorBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/EditorBridge#togglebold).

To build your own button, read the state with `useBridgeState`:

```tsx
const BoldButton = ({ editor }: { editor: EditorBridge }) => {
  const { isBoldActive, canToggleBold } = useBridgeState(editor);
  return (
    <Button
      title={isBoldActive ? 'Unbold' : 'Bold'}
      disabled={!canToggleBold}
      onPress={() => editor.toggleBold()}
    />
  );
};
```

1.0 reported `Property 'toggleBold' does not exist on type 'EditorBridge'` with deep imports from `@10play/tentap-editor/src/...` or with `moduleResolution: "node"`. 1.1 fixes this. Importing from `@10play/tentap-editor` is still recommended.

### Lists rendered with `react-native-render-html` have extra space

TipTap wraps the content of every list item in a paragraph (`<li><p>…</p></li>`). `react-native-render-html` gives each `<p>` its default margins. Remove them for paragraphs inside list items with a custom renderer; see [Rendering editor HTML](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/renderHtml).

### How do I put the editor inside a `ScrollView`?

Turn on `dynamicHeight` so the editor is as tall as its content, and call `useScrollToCaret` so your `ScrollView` keeps the caret above the keyboard:

```tsx
const Form = () => {
  const editor = useEditorBridge({ dynamicHeight: true });
  const scrollViewRef = useRef<ScrollView>(null);
  useScrollToCaret(editor, scrollViewRef);

  return (
    <EditorKeyboardAvoidingView style={{ flex: 1 }}>
      <ScrollView ref={scrollViewRef} keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled">
        <TextInput placeholder="Title" />
        <RichText editor={editor} />
      </ScrollView>
    </EditorKeyboardAvoidingView>
  );
};
```

See [Editor inside a ScrollView](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/scrollView), including how to cap the editor's height.

### Images inside a paragraph are moved out of it

Images are block nodes by default. Configure the `ImageBridge` to make them inline:

```tsx
const editor = useEditorBridge({
  bridgeExtensions: [
    ...TenTapStartKit,
    ImageBridge.configureExtension({ inline: true }),
  ],
});
```

See [Inline images](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/configureExtensions#inline-images).

### How do I use a custom font?

Load it with an `@font-face` rule in `CoreBridge.configureCSS`, either from a local file (recommended for large fonts) or embedded as base64. See [Adding custom fonts](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/customCss#adding-custom-fonts). For Chinese, Japanese and Korean text that doesn't turn bold or italic, see [CJK text](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/customCss#chinese-japanese-and-korean-text).

### The toolbar is hidden behind the keyboard, or floats above it

Use `EditorKeyboardAvoidingView` instead of React Native's `KeyboardAvoidingView`. It measures how far the keyboard reaches into it, so it needs no `keyboardVerticalOffset` and also works below a header, above a tab bar and on edge-to-edge Android. See [Keyboard and caret](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/setup/keyboard).

### The line I'm typing goes under the toolbar

`RichText` measures the keyboard and the library's `Toolbar` and keeps the caret above them. Mark your own toolbar with [useKeyboardAccessory](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/CustomKeyboardUtils#usekeyboardaccessory). For other views over the editor, set [scrollBottomOffset](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/useEditorBridge#scrollbottomoffset).

### Do I have to wait for `isReady` before calling editor methods?

No. Commands called before the editor has loaded are queued and sent in order once it is ready. `getHTML` and the other async methods wait for the editor too; set [rpcTimeoutMs](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/useEditorBridge#rpctimeoutms) if they should give up.

### Spaces in my HTML disappear

ProseMirror collapses runs of whitespace in HTML. Pass `parseOptions: { preserveWhitespace: 'full' }` to `useEditorBridge` or to `setContent`. See [Keeping whitespace](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/workingWithContent#keeping-whitespace).

### Do custom keyboards work in Expo Go?

Yes, with a JavaScript fallback driver. A development build uses the native driver. See [Expo Go and the fallback driver](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/customKeyboard#expo-go-and-the-fallback-driver).

### How do I show the content read-only?

Pass `editable: false` to `useEditorBridge`. Changing it later calls `editor.setEditable`. To show saved HTML outside an editor, see [Rendering editor HTML](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/renderHtml).

---

Source: https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/setup/installation

# Installation

## React Native

```bash
yarn add @10play/tentap-editor react-native-webview
cd ios && pod install
```

Then rebuild your app (`yarn ios` / `yarn android`).

The package contains a small native module (`TenTapKeyboard`) used by [custom keyboards](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/customKeyboard). It is autolinked: `pod install` adds it on iOS and Gradle picks it up on Android, with no changes to your native code. The editor itself doesn't depend on it. If it is missing, for example in a build made before you installed the package, everything keeps working and custom keyboards use a JavaScript fallback driver.

After upgrading the package, run `pod install` again and rebuild, so the native module matches the JavaScript.

## Expo

```bash
npx expo install @10play/tentap-editor react-native-webview
```

- **Development build / prebuild (recommended):** everything works, including the native keyboard driver. No config plugin is needed. Rebuild your [development build](https://docs.expo.dev/develop/development-builds/introduction/) (`npx expo run:ios`, `npx expo run:android`, or EAS) after installing or upgrading. If you commit the native folders, run `npx expo prebuild` again.
- **Expo Go:** the editor works. Expo Go can't load the native module, so custom keyboards use the JavaScript fallback driver automatically (see [Expo Go and the fallback driver](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/customKeyboard#expo-go-and-the-fallback-driver)). Expo Go also ships its own react-native-webview version, so test [an editor inside a ScrollView](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/scrollView) in a development build.

The [advanced setup](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/setup/advancedSetup) also needs a development build.

Now you're ready to add tentap to your app! Continue with [Keyboard and caret](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/setup/keyboard) for the screen layout, or jump to the [basic example](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/basic).

## Requirements

| | Supported |
| --- | --- |
| React Native | JavaScript: any version supported by `react-native-webview`. Native module: **0.74 or newer**, old and new architecture (bridge and bridgeless). |
| Expo | SDK 51 or newer for development builds and prebuild. Expo Go is supported with the keyboard fallback. |
| react-native-webview | 13.7 or newer. Use **13.13.3 or newer** on the new architecture if the editor is inside a `ScrollView` (see [Editor inside a ScrollView](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/scrollView)). |
| iOS | 15.1 or newer (or your app's `min_ios_version_supported`) |
| Android | The library builds with `minSdkVersion` 24. The editor is tested on Android 10 (API level 29) and newer, which we recommend as your minimum. `androidKeyboardMode="stable"` needs Android 11 (API level 30). |

The React Native 0.74 floor is documented here and isn't enforced by the package. The Android native module needs `BaseReactPackage` (added in React Native 0.74) and doesn't compile on older versions. The peer dependencies (`react`, `react-native`, `react-native-webview`) are all `*`, as in 1.0, so your package manager won't warn you. Stay on 1.0.x if you can't upgrade React Native.

The TipTap packages, `@tiptap/react`, `react-dom` and `lodash` are regular dependencies and are installed for you. If your app also targets the web or builds a [custom editor bundle](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/setup/advancedSetup), keep a `react-dom` that matches your `react` in your own `package.json`.

## Example apps

The repository has two example apps:

- [`example/`](https://github.com/10play/10tap-editor/tree/main/example): React Native CLI (React Native 0.81), built on both the new and the old architecture. It has every example in these docs, including the advanced setup.
- [`example-expo/`](https://github.com/10play/10tap-editor/tree/main/example-expo): Expo with a development build. It also runs on the web.

### Expo Web

For expo-web support follow this [guide](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/setup/expoWeb)
