# Keyboard and caret

This page shows the screen layout that keeps the toolbar on top of the keyboard and the line being typed above the toolbar, on iOS and Android, with or without a navigation header, on edge-to-edge Android and with custom keyboards.

## Recommended layout

Wrap the editor and the toolbar in an `EditorKeyboardAvoidingView`:

```tsx
import React from 'react';
import { StyleSheet, View } from 'react-native';
import { SafeAreaView } from 'react-native-safe-area-context';
import {
  EditorKeyboardAvoidingView,
  RichText,
  Toolbar,
  useEditorBridge,
} from '@10play/tentap-editor';

export const Editor = () => {
  const editor = useEditorBridge({
    autofocus: true,
    avoidIosKeyboard: true,
    initialContent: '<p>Start editing!</p>',
  });

  return (
    <SafeAreaView style={styles.fullScreen}>
      <EditorKeyboardAvoidingView style={styles.fullScreen}>
        <View style={styles.fullScreen}>
          <RichText editor={editor} />
        </View>
        <View style={styles.toolbarRow}>
          <Toolbar editor={editor} />
        </View>
      </EditorKeyboardAvoidingView>
    </SafeAreaView>
  );
};

const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  fullScreen: {
    flex: 1,
  },
  // The toolbar's default flex: 1 would share the column with the editor;
  // in a row it only fills the width.
  toolbarRow: {
    flexDirection: 'row',
  },
});
```

[EditorKeyboardAvoidingView](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/CustomKeyboardUtils#editorkeyboardavoidingview) measures where it ends in the window and pads its bottom by the part of it that the keyboard covers. The editor gets shorter, and the toolbar sits right on the keyboard:

- **No `keyboardVerticalOffset`.** It works below a navigation header, above a tab bar and inside a `SafeAreaView`, because it measures its real position instead of relying on an offset.
- **Edge-to-edge Android.** This is the default in Expo SDK 53+, and for apps targeting SDK 35+ on Android 15+. The keyboard there also covers the navigation bar, and React Native's keyboard height leaves that out. `EditorKeyboardAvoidingView` measures against the top of the keyboard, so the toolbar isn't partly hidden. This also works without the native module (Expo Go).
- **`adjustResize`.** When the window already shrinks for the keyboard, it adds no padding.
- **Custom keyboards.** The padding stays the same while you switch between the system keyboard and a [custom keyboard](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/customKeyboard), so the toolbar doesn't move.

The `Toolbar` shows itself while the editor is focused and a keyboard is up. Pass `hidden` to control this yourself.

The same layout works below a `react-navigation` header with no changes; see [Navigation header](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/navHeader).

### The 1.0 layout

The layout from the 1.0 docs still works: a React Native `KeyboardAvoidingView` with `behavior="padding"`, absolutely positioned at the bottom of the screen, around the `Toolbar`. It needs a `keyboardVerticalOffset` below a header. On edge-to-edge Android it can leave the toolbar partly behind the keyboard. You can switch to `EditorKeyboardAvoidingView` without other changes, and it accepts the same absolute style:

```tsx
<EditorKeyboardAvoidingView
  style={{ position: 'absolute', width: '100%', bottom: 0 }}
>
  <Toolbar editor={editor} />
</EditorKeyboardAvoidingView>;
```

## Keeping the caret visible

You don't need any `paddingBottom` for the caret. While a keyboard is up, `RichText` measures how far the keyboard and the toolbar on it reach into the editor. It then keeps the line being typed about one line above the toolbar, also when the keyboard grows (an emoji or suggestion bar), after an image is inserted, after a keyboard switch, and in an editor that ends above the keyboard. See [avoidIosKeyboard](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/useEditorBridge#avoidioskeyboard) for the details.

- **Your own toolbar.** If you draw your own toolbar on the keyboard, mark it with [useKeyboardAccessory](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/CustomKeyboardUtils#usekeyboardaccessory) so its height is measured exactly. The library's `Toolbar` does this itself.
- **Other views over the editor.** For views that `RichText` can't measure, such as a floating button over the bottom of the editor, keep extra space below the caret with [scrollBottomOffset](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/useEditorBridge#scrollbottomoffset):

  ```tsx
  const editor = useEditorBridge({ scrollBottomOffset: 60 });
  ```

- **`updateScrollThresholdAndMargin`** still works, but `RichText` overwrites the value when the keyboard opens or closes. Use `scrollBottomOffset` for a value that has to stay.

## Editor inside a ScrollView

A [dynamicHeight](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/useEditorBridge#dynamicheight) editor grows with its content and doesn't scroll itself. Use [useScrollToCaret](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/CustomKeyboardUtils#usescrolltocaret) so that your `ScrollView` keeps the caret above the keyboard. See [Editor inside a ScrollView](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/scrollView).

## Android window modes

| Window | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Edge-to-edge (Expo SDK 53+; `targetSdk` 35+ on Android 15+) | The window never resizes. `EditorKeyboardAvoidingView` pads for the keyboard and the navigation bar under it. |
| `adjustResize` (React Native's default without edge-to-edge) | The window shrinks for the system keyboard, and `EditorKeyboardAvoidingView` adds no padding for it. While switching to a custom keyboard, the toolbar can move for a moment; see [keeping the toolbar still](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/customKeyboard#android-keeping-the-toolbar-still). |
| `adjustNothing` / `androidKeyboardMode="stable"` | The keyboard covers the window, as on iOS. |

## Reading the keyboard state

[useKeyboard](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/CustomKeyboardUtils#usekeyboard) returns whether a keyboard (system or custom) is up, its height, how far it covers the window (`keyboardCoverHeight`) and where its top is (`keyboardTop`). Use it to build your own keyboard-aware views.

---

Source: https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/setup/advancedSetup

# Advanced Setup

Make sure you read the core concepts page before setup advance and check if the simple usage is good enough for you.

See full working example here https://github.com/10play/10TapAdvancedExample

## Setting Up Our Custom Editor Directory

### Step 1 - creating the directory

Create a new folder in your project called `editor-web` (or any other name) - advance setup will let you full control on what running inside the editor webview, so we need to create a separate folder that will include code that will run inside the webview and will have different build process and tsconfig

### Step 2 - adding tsconfig

Create `editor-web/tsconfig.json`:

```ts title="editor-web/tsconfig.json"
{
  "$schema": "https://json.schemastore.org/tsconfig",
  "_version": "2.0.0",
  "compilerOptions": {
    "lib": ["dom", "dom.iterable", "esnext"],
    "module": "esnext",
    "paths": {
      "@10play/tentap-editor": [
        "../node_modules/@10play/tentap-editor/lib-web/typescript/webEditorUtils/index.d.ts"
      ]
    },
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "target": "es2015",
    "allowJs": true,
    "allowSyntheticDefaultImports": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true,
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "noEmit": true,
    "noFallthroughCasesInSwitch": true,
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "strict": true
  }
}
```

It's important to configure `paths` so on web the web types will be used instead of native types.

### Step 3 - updating root tsconfig

Add exclude on the root tsconfig.json: `"exclude": ["./editor-web"]`

### Step 4 - Add index.html AdvancedEditor.tsx and index.tsx

Add the following files

```html title="index.html"
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
    <title>RichTextEditor</title>
  </head>
  <style>
    body {
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
    }
    #root > div:nth-of-type(1) {
      position: absolute;
      height: 100%;
      overflow: auto;
      width: 100%;
      top: 0;
      bottom: 0;
    }
    #root > div.dynamic-height {
      height: unset;
    }

    #root div .ProseMirror {
      min-height: 100%;
      overflow: visible;
    }
    #root div.dynamic-height .ProseMirror {
      height: auto;
      min-height: 0;
      display: flow-root;
    }
    .ProseMirror:focus {
      outline: none;
    }
    .highlight-background {
      background-color: #e6e6ff;
    }
  </style>
  <body>
    <div id="root"></div>
    <script type="module" src="/index.tsx"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

```tsx title="AdvancedEditor.tsx"
import React from 'react';
import { EditorContent, useTenTap, TenTapStartKit } from '@10play/tentap-editor';
import { CounterBridge } from '../CounterBridge';
import Document from '@tiptap/extension-document';
import Paragraph from '@tiptap/extension-paragraph';
import Text from '@tiptap/extension-text';

/**
 * Here we control the web side of our custom editor
 */
export const AdvancedEditor = () => {
  const editor = useTenTap({
    bridges: [...TenTapStartKit, CounterBridge],
    tiptapOptions: {
      extensions: [Document, Paragraph, Text],
    },
  });
  return (
    <EditorContent
      editor={editor}
      className={window.dynamicHeight ? 'dynamic-height' : undefined}
    />
  );
};
```

```tsx title="index.tsx"
import React from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { AdvancedEditor } from './AdvancedEditor';

/**
 * This is the entrypoint for the "web" part of our editor that will be built with vite
 */

declare global {
  interface Window {
    contentInjected: boolean | undefined;
  }
}

/**
 * On android - react-native-webview there is a bug where sometimes the content
 * is injected after the window is loaded https://github.com/react-native-webview/react-native-webview/pull/2960
 * To overcome this we will check if the content is injected before rendering the editor
 */
const contentInjected = () => window.contentInjected;
let interval: NodeJS.Timeout;
interval = setInterval(() => {
  if (!contentInjected()) return;
  // Once content is injected into the webview, we can render the editor
  const container = document.getElementById('root');
  const root = createRoot(container!);
  root.render(<AdvancedEditor />);
  clearInterval(interval);
  return;
}, 1);
```

### Step 5 - adding a bundler

We chose to use vite as our bundler so first run

```bash
yarn add -D vite @vitejs/plugin-react vite-plugin-singlefile
```

And now let's create `vite.config.ts` and configure it

```ts title="vite.config.ts"
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';
import { viteSingleFile } from 'vite-plugin-singlefile';

// This config is used to build the web editor into a single file

export default defineConfig({
  root: 'src/editor-web', // This should be the directory of your index.html
  build: {
    outDir: 'build',
  },
  resolve: {
    alias: [
      {
        find: '@10play/tentap-editor', // On our web bundle we only want to include web related code
        replacement: '@10play/tentap-editor/web',
      },
      // We alias tiptap view and state to use the internal version of tiptap to avoid this error https://github.com/ueberdostiptap/issues/3869#issuecomment-2167931620
      {
        find: '@tiptap/pm/view',
        replacement: '@10play/tentap-editor/web',
      },
      {
        find: '@tiptap/pm/state',
        replacement: '@10play/tentap-editor/web',
      },
    ],
  },
  plugins: [react(), viteSingleFile()],
  server: {
    port: 3000,
  },
});
```

> It's important to have the `alias` configuration so vite will not load react-native code

#### Sharing tiptap with `@10play/tentap-editor/web`

`@10play/tentap-editor/web` is a prebuilt bundle with its own copy of tiptap and ProseMirror inlined. Code you import from `@tiptap/*` in your editor-web, such as extra extensions, is bundled separately, and the two copies don't recognize each other's objects. Bundler options such as vite's `resolve.dedupe` cannot merge them, because the copy inside `@10play/tentap-editor/web` is not a package in `node_modules`.

- Import `EditorContent` (and `useEditor` if you need it) from `@10play/tentap-editor`, not from `@tiptap/react`, so the editor and the component that renders it come from the same copy.
- Keep the `@tiptap/pm/view` and `@tiptap/pm/state` aliases above, so extensions share ProseMirror's view and state classes with the bundled editor.
- Install extra `@tiptap/*` extensions at the same version that `@10play/tentap-editor` uses (`npm ls @tiptap/core` shows it).

### Step 6 - adding build scripts

Add scripts on package.json so it will be easy to run/build editor-web:

```ts title="package.json"
"scripts": {
    ...
    "editor:dev": "vite --config ./editor-web/vite.config.ts",
    "editor:build": "vite --config ./editor-web/vite.config.ts build && yarn editor:post-build",
    "editor:post-build":"node ./node_modules/@10play/tentap-editor/scripts/buildEditor.js ./editor-web/build/index.html",
    "reverse-android": "adb reverse tcp:3000 tcp:3000",
}
```

`editor:dev` - Run the editor web in dev mode  
`editor:build` - Build the editor web, probably need to add to your deploy/build process  
`editor:post-build` - This will take your built html file, and paste into a a ts and exports a string `editorHtml`  
 which we can then later use as the source of our RichText.  
`reverse-android` - On android need to reverse ports so it will be able to work with DEV / DEV_SERVER_URL props

### Step 7 - using our custom editor

`Outside` of editor-web update your `EditorBridge` to used the html we just built.

```tsx
import { editorHtml } from './editor-web/build/editorHtml';
const editor = useEditorBridge({
  customSource: editorHtml,
  // ...your other options
});
```

### Step 8 - Install react-dom

`yarn add react-dom`

`yarn add -D @types/react-dom`

Install the `react-dom` version that matches your `react`.

You basically done with the advance setup now you have full control of the editor-web you can write your own bridgeExtensions add additional tiptapExtensions

## useTenTap

`useTenTap` creates the TipTap editor inside the WebView and connects it to React Native.

```ts
import { TenTapStartKit, useTenTap } from '@10play/tentap-editor';
import Document from '@tiptap/extension-document';
import Paragraph from '@tiptap/extension-paragraph';
import Text from '@tiptap/extension-text';
import { CounterBridge } from '../CounterBridge';

const editor = useTenTap({
  bridges: [...TenTapStartKit, CounterBridge],
  tiptapOptions: { extensions: [Document, Paragraph, Text] },
});
```

- `bridges`: the bridges the editor-web knows about. A bridge with a TipTap extension is enabled when the native side's `bridgeExtensions` contains a bridge with the same name. A bridge without one, such as a bridge that only adds to the editor state or handles your own messages, always runs. Bridges and extensions are resolved once, when the editor is created.
- `tiptapOptions`: options passed to TipTap's `useEditor`. Its `extensions` are added after the bridges' extensions. The event handlers `onUpdate`, `onSelectionUpdate` and `onTransaction` run **after** tentap's own handlers instead of replacing them, and `onCreate` is yours alone (tentap no longer uses it to announce the editor), so none of them can break the connection to React Native. Every other option, such as `content`, `editable`, `parseOptions`, `editorProps` or `shouldRerenderOnTransaction`, overrides tentap's default.
- `stateUpdateDebounceMs`: how long editor state updates are debounced before they are sent to React Native. default: `10`. The first state update after the editor is created is always sent right away.

`useTenTap` returns the TipTap `Editor` (or `null` before it exists). Its options type is exported as `UseTenTapArgs`.

## Upgrading your editor-web

Rebuild your editor bundle (`yarn editor:build`) whenever you upgrade `@10play/tentap-editor`. Bundles built with an older version keep working, but miss the newer web-side features: `insertContent`, `getSelectedText`, `parseOptions`, and the dynamic height and readiness fixes. `getSelectedText` rejects with `TentapUnsupportedError` on such a bundle.

When upgrading from 1.0, also:

- change `#root div.dynamic-height .ProseMirror` in your `index.html` to `height: auto; min-height: 0; display: flow-root;` as shown above, so dynamic height can shrink, doesn't loop on iOS and includes the first and last paragraph margins (1.1 also injects this rule, so a bundle that wasn't rebuilt yet gets it too);
- preferably import `EditorContent` from `@10play/tentap-editor` instead of `@tiptap/react`, and follow [Sharing tiptap](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/setup/advancedSetup#sharing-tiptap-with-10playtentap-editorweb).

The `contentInjected` polling in `index.tsx` still works. In 1.1 the configuration is written into the `customSource` HTML before your script runs, so the first check already passes.

## Alternative Setup

> **Info**
>
> In case you are using Expo you have to use this Alternative Setup for dev mode on your advance setup editor
>

There is an alternative vite setup that does not require a vite dev server as suggested in [#80](https://github.com/10play/10tap-editor/issues/80). This setup does not require we add the `DEV` prop

### Update vite.config.ts

In `vite.config.ts`, add a plugin that runs `editor:post-build` after every build, and set `emptyOutDir: false`:

```ts title="vite.config.ts"
import { exec } from 'child_process';
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react';
import { viteSingleFile } from 'vite-plugin-singlefile';

export default defineConfig({
  root: 'src/editor-web',
  build: {
    outDir: 'build',
    emptyOutDir: false,
  },
  resolve: {
    // the same aliases as above
  },
  plugins: [
    react(),
    viteSingleFile(),
    {
      name: 'postbuild-commands',
      closeBundle: async () => {
        exec('yarn editor:post-build', (error) => {
          if (error) console.error(`exec error: ${error}`);
        });
      },
    },
  ],
});
```

### Update package.json

Update the `editor:dev` script to watch the advanced editor instead of running a dev-server, the hot reload will be handled by metro and not vite.

`"editor:dev": "vite --config ./editor-web/vite.config.ts -w build"`

---

Source: https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/setup/expoWeb

# Expo Web Setup (Beta)

Some additional steps are necessary for supporting expo web. The [`example-expo`](https://github.com/10play/10tap-editor/tree/main/example-expo) app in the repository runs on the web with this setup (`yarn example:expo web`); there is also a standalone example [here](https://github.com/10play/10tap-web-example).

### Step 1 - Install required deps

`npx expo install @10play/react-native-web-webview react-native-web react-dom expo-crypto`

`expo-crypto` and the `crypto` alias below are only needed by older versions of `@10play/react-native-web-webview`; the `example-expo` app runs version 0.0.3 without them. Keeping them does no harm.

Several editors on one page work with any version of `@10play/react-native-web-webview`: the shim delivers every editor's messages to every WebView on the page, so 1.1 tags each message with an editor id and every editor ignores messages meant for another one. A custom `onMessage` on `RichText` only receives its own editor's messages too.

### Step 2 - Configuring your bundler

Which bundler are you using?

**Metro**

Create config file if not already `npx expo customize metro.config.js`

Into your `metro.config.js` add the following configuration

```js
const { getDefaultConfig } = require('expo/metro-config');

/** @type {import('expo/metro-config').MetroConfig} */
const config = getDefaultConfig(__dirname);

const webAliases = {
  'react-native': 'react-native-web',
  'react-native-webview': '@10play/react-native-web-webview',
  'react-native/Libraries/Utilities/codegenNativeComponent':
    '@10play/react-native-web-webview/shim',
  'crypto': 'expo-crypto',
};

config.resolver.resolveRequest = (
  context,
  realModuleName,
  platform,
  moduleName
) => {
  if (platform === 'web') {
    const alias = webAliases[realModuleName];
    if (alias) {
      return {
        filePath: require.resolve(alias),
        type: 'sourceFile',
      };
    }
  }
  return context.resolveRequest(context, realModuleName, platform, moduleName);
};

module.exports = config;
```

**Webpack**

Create config file if not already `npx expo customize webpack.config.js`

Into your `webpack.config.js` add the following configuration

```js
const createExpoWebpackConfigAsync = require('@expo/webpack-config');

module.exports = async function (env, argv) {
  const config = await createExpoWebpackConfigAsync(env, argv);

  // Alias react-native-webview and crypto
  config.resolve.alias = {
    ...config.resolve.alias,
    'react-native': 'react-native-web',
    'react-native-webview': '@10play/react-native-web-webview',
    'crypto': 'expo-crypto',
  };

  // Shim codegenNativeComponent
  config.resolve.fallback = {
    ...config.resolve.fallback,
    'react-native/Libraries/Utilities/codegenNativeComponent':
      '@10play/react-native-web-webview/shim',
  };

  return config;
};
```

### Step 3 - Restart Metro

Restart metro for changes to take effect and the editor should load

## Notes

- `dynamicHeight` works on web: the height is applied to the iframe's `style`, which is the only style the shim reads.
- [Custom keyboards](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/customKeyboard) render under the toolbar, but the browser's own keyboard isn't hidden on web. They use the JavaScript driver; there is no native module on web.
- On web the `Toolbar` renders its items without a `FlatList`, so `ListComponent` isn't used.

---

Source: https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/migrations/v1.1

# Migrating to v1.1

1.1 is a minor release: nothing public was removed, and code written for 1.0 keeps compiling and running. **No code changes are required.** It rebuilds the editor core, fixes a long list of bugs, adds a few options and methods, and brings back custom keyboards. This page lists the upgrade steps, the optional improvements, and what behaves differently.

## Upgrade steps

1. Update the package (and react-native-webview, if it is older than 13.7):

   ```bash
   yarn add @10play/tentap-editor@^1.1.0
   ```

2. Rebuild your native app. 1.1 contains a small autolinked native module (`TenTapKeyboard`), used by custom keyboards. Until you rebuild, the editor works and custom keyboards use the JavaScript fallback driver.
   - iOS: `cd ios && pod install`
   - Android: a new Gradle build
   - Expo: `npx expo prebuild`, or rebuild your dev client. Expo Go keeps working without a rebuild.
3. If you use the [advanced setup](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/setup/advancedSetup), rebuild your editor bundle and follow [Upgrading your editor-web](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/setup/advancedSetup#upgrading-your-editor-web).
4. Coming from 0.7.x, also follow the [1.0 migration guide](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/migrations/v1.0). In particular, TipTap v3 renamed History to UndoRedo, so `HistoryBridge` is named `undoRedo`; code that looks bridges up by `'history'` must use `'undoRedo'`. 1.1 also sends the bridge's config under `history`, so a custom editor bundle built with 0.7.x still receives it.

## Requirements

- **React Native 0.74 or newer** (Expo SDK 51 or newer) for the native module. The Android module is built on `BaseReactPackage`, which was added in 0.74, so the Android build fails on older versions. The `react-native` peer dependency is still `*`, so package managers don't check this. Stay on 1.0.x if you can't upgrade React Native.
- **react-native-webview 13.7 or newer.** Use 13.13.3 or newer on the new architecture if the editor is inside a `ScrollView`.
- The Android package is still `com.tentap.TenTapViewPackage`, now written in Java. The library no longer applies the Kotlin Gradle plugin, which conflicted with AGP 9's built-in Kotlin support.
- `package.json` declares a `codegenConfig` again (`RNTenTapSpec`, a native module). If a build fails on stale codegen output after upgrading, clean the build folders (`ios/build`, `android/app/build`) and rebuild.
- `@tiptap/react` and `react-dom` are still dependencies, so a 1.0 advanced setup that imports `EditorContent` from `@tiptap/react` keeps building. Importing it from `@10play/tentap-editor` instead is recommended ([Sharing tiptap](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/setup/advancedSetup#sharing-tiptap-with-10playtentap-editorweb)).
- The `react-dom` dependency accepts React 18 or 19 (`^18.2.0 || ^19.0.0`) instead of only 18, so it can share your app's `react-dom` instead of installing a second copy. If your app targets the web or builds a custom editor bundle, keep a `react-dom` that matches your `react` in your own `package.json`.

## Optional: the new keyboard layout

The 1.0 layout, a `KeyboardAvoidingView` around the `Toolbar` with a `keyboardVerticalOffset` below a header, keeps working. 1.1 adds `EditorKeyboardAvoidingView`, which needs no offset and also keeps the toolbar on the keyboard on edge-to-edge Android (the default in Expo SDK 53+). Swapping it in is a one-line change; see [Keyboard and caret](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/setup/keyboard).

## Custom keyboards are back

`CustomKeyboard`, `ColorKeyboard`, `CustomKeyboardExtension`, the `colorKeyboard` theme and the `Color` / `ColorKeyboardTheme` types are exported again. See [Custom Keyboard Utils](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/CustomKeyboardUtils).

Coming from 0.7.x:

- Your code compiles unchanged. `rootRef` is ignored and can be removed.
- The keyboard component is now rendered in your app's own React tree. It can use your context providers and hooks, including `useBridgeState(editor)` to follow the editor state. It also receives `editor`, `close` and `keyboardHeight` props.
- It works on the new architecture, including bridgeless mode and the React Native 0.79+ app templates.
- `TenTapView` is a deprecated component that renders nothing. Remove it.
- `colorKeyboard` is optional on `EditorTheme`, so a full theme object written for 1.0 still type-checks. `editor.theme`, `defaultEditorTheme` and `darkEditorTheme` are typed with it, so `editor.theme.colorKeyboard.keyboardRootColor` compiles as in 0.7.x.
- The toolbar stays visible while a custom keyboard is open, so you can drop the `hidden` logic from the 0.7.x examples.

## New options and methods

| | |
| --- | --- |
| [`parseOptions`](../api/useEditorBridge.md#parseoptions) | ProseMirror parse options, e.g. to keep whitespace |
| [`scrollBottomOffset`](../api/useEditorBridge.md#scrollbottomoffset) | extra space kept below the cursor |
| [`avoidKeyboard`](../api/useEditorBridge.md#avoidkeyboard) | alias of `avoidIosKeyboard` |
| [`mergeStyles`](../api/useEditorBridge.md#mergestyles) | merge the `RichText` `style` prop instead of replacing |
| [`rpcTimeoutMs`](../api/useEditorBridge.md#rpctimeoutms) | timeout for `getHTML` and the other async methods |
| [`insertContent`](../api/EditorBridge.md#insertcontent) | insert HTML, text or JSON at the cursor |
| [`getSelectedText`](../api/EditorBridge.md#getselectedtext) | read the selected text |
| [`setContent(content, options)`](../api/EditorBridge.md#setcontent) | `parseOptions` and `emitUpdate` per call |
| [`Toolbar` `headingItems`](../api/Components.md#customizing-the-heading-toolbar) | customize the heading toolbar; `HEADING_ITEMS` and `ToolbarContext` are exported |
| `TentapRpcTimeoutError`, `TentapUnsupportedError` | [errors](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/EditorBridge#errors) thrown by the async methods |
| `useRemoteEditorBridge` | subscribes to the most recently created editor |
| [`Toolbar` `ListComponent`](../api/Components.md#toolbar) | render the toolbar with another list component, such as a bottom-sheet `FlatList` |
| [`linkBarTheme.hintText`](../examples/customTheme.md#link-bar) | placeholder of the link bar input |
| [`useTenTap` `stateUpdateDebounceMs`](../setup/advancedSetup.md#usetentap) | debounce of state updates from a custom editor bundle |

## Behaviour changes

These are fixes, but they change what some apps observe.

**Editor identity**

- `useEditorBridge` returns the same object on every render, so it is safe in dependency arrays; its option fields (`theme`, `dynamicHeight`, …) always read the latest render. `RichText` and `Toolbar` re-render when the options change, also under a `React.memo` parent. Your own memoized components that render from `editor.theme` or another option should take that value as a prop, since `editor` alone no longer changes.

**Readiness and messaging**

- `isReady` becomes `true` as soon as the editor is created, also when it is not editable and not focused. It goes back to `false` while the WebView reloads.
- Commands called before the editor is ready are queued and sent in order once it is ready. They used to be dropped with an "Editor isn't ready yet" warning.
- The web editor sends `editor-ready` followed by a full `stateUpdate` as soon as it is created.
- If you read messages in your own `onMessage`: messages can carry extra fields (`editorId`, `v`) besides `type` and `payload`, `editor-ready` has a payload, and there are new message types (`boot-error`, `tentap-editor-press`). Ignore what you don't use. A development warning is logged when `onMessage` is passed without `exclusivelyUseCustomOnMessage`; the default is still `true`.
- If the WebView's content process is killed, the editor reloads and restores its content and settings. Edits made since the content was last read can be lost.
- On iOS, the WebView is remounted after its first load only with react-native-webview 13.12.3 and 13.12.4, which need the workaround.
- `useEditorContent` fetches the content when it changes, not on every selection change.
- Bridge configs containing quotes or `</script>` no longer break the editor.

**Layout**

- `style` and `containerStyle` passed to `RichText` still replace the editor's own styles, as in 1.0, unless you set the new `mergeStyles` option. The difference: with `dynamicHeight`, the content height is now applied after your `containerStyle`, so your styles can no longer switch dynamic height off by accident.
- `RichText` throws a clear error when `editor` doesn't come from `useEditorBridge`. A spread copy such as `{ ...editor }` still works, as in 1.0, but its option fields are a snapshot, so prefer passing `editor` itself.
- `dynamicHeight` works in any parent, shrinks when content is deleted, keeps the scroll position when the height is capped, and no longer adds keyboard padding.

**Keyboard and caret**

- `RichText` measures how far the keyboard and the toolbar on it reach into the editor, and keeps the line being typed about one line above the toolbar. In 1.0 the inset was derived from the keyboard height (iOS) or a fixed toolbar height (Android), so the caret could end up under the toolbar. The document padding and the scroll threshold now come from this measurement.
- This applies to every editor without `dynamicHeight` while a keyboard is up, also without `avoidIosKeyboard`. An editor that ends above the keyboard keeps about one line of space below the caret. Until the first measurement, `avoidIosKeyboard` keeps its 1.0 value.
- A toolbar of your own on the keyboard that isn't marked with [useKeyboardAccessory](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/CustomKeyboardUtils#usekeyboardaccessory) gets the default toolbar height of room.
- `useKeyboard()` keeps `keyboardHeight` while switching between the system and a custom keyboard, and returns new fields. `isKeyboardUp` and `keyboardHeight` behave as in 1.0 when no custom keyboard is used.

**Editing**

- `setImage` adds an empty paragraph after an image that ends the document and moves the cursor there.
- Links without a scheme get `https://` (`www.google.com` → `https://www.google.com`), or the `defaultProtocol` passed to `LinkBridge.configureExtension`. Plain email addresses get `mailto:`.
- CSS injected with `injectCSS` is re-applied when the WebView reloads.

**Toolbar**

- `shouldHideDisabledToolbarItems` also hides disabled heading items.
- The link bar no longer closes when its input loses focus. The keyboard's Done key inserts the link.
- Each toolbar context renders its own list, so the heading toolbar opens scrolled to the start.

**Advanced setup**

- `tiptapOptions.onCreate`, `onUpdate`, `onSelectionUpdate` and `onTransaction` passed to `useTenTap` run in addition to tentap's handlers instead of replacing them. If you overrode them on purpose to stop tentap's messages, that no longer works.
- Bridges and extensions are resolved once, when the editor is created.

## Type-level changes

- `EditorBridge` (with `CoreBridge`) has two new required members, `insertContent` and `getSelectedText`. If you build `EditorBridge` objects by hand, for example as test mocks, add them.
- `setContent` has a new optional second parameter.
- `EditorTheme` has a new optional `colorKeyboard` key.
- The source types are self-contained: deep imports from `@10play/tentap-editor/src/...` and `moduleResolution: "node"` no longer report missing bridge methods such as `toggleBold`. Importing from the package root is still recommended.
- `extendEditorInstance` receives an optional sixth argument, `BridgeContext`. Existing five-argument bridges are unaffected.

## Deprecations

| Deprecated | Use instead |
| --- | --- |
| `CustomKeyboard` `rootRef` prop | nothing, it's ignored |
| `TenTapView` | nothing, it renders nothing |
| `CustomKeyboard` `onKeyboardHideAndroid` prop | `onClose` |

Deprecated APIs keep working in 1.x. `avoidIosKeyboard` is not deprecated; `avoidKeyboard` is an alias with a clearer name.

---

Source: https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/migrations/v1.0

# Migrating to v1.0

This guide will help you migrate from pre-1.0 versions to v1.0 of 10tap-editor.

## Breaking Changes

### Custom Keyboard Removed

> **Tip**
> Custom keyboards are back in 1.1, with the same API. See the [1.1 migration guide](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/migrations/v1.1).

The custom keyboard functionality has been removed in v1.0. This includes:

- `CustomKeyboard` component
- `CustomKeyboardUtils` API
- `ColorKeyboard` and `CustomKeyboardExtension`
- the `TenTapView` native component
- the `colorKeyboard` key of `EditorTheme`, and the `Color` and `ColorKeyboardTheme` types
- the `codegenConfig` entry (`RNTenTapViewSpec`) in the package's `package.json`
- Color keyboard example
- Custom keyboard example

### HistoryBridge Renamed

TipTap v3 renamed its History extension to UndoRedo, so `HistoryBridge` is now named `undoRedo` instead of `history`. Code that looks bridges up by name, such as `TenTapStartKit.filter((b) => b.name !== 'history')`, must use `'undoRedo'`. Custom editor bundles built with 0.7.x didn't receive the HistoryBridge config from a 1.0 app; 1.1 sends it under both names.

### KeyboardAvoidingView Behavior Changed

The `behavior` prop for `KeyboardAvoidingView` has been simplified in v1.0.

**Before (Pre-1.0):**
```tsx
<KeyboardAvoidingView
  behavior={Platform.OS === 'ios' ? 'padding' : 'height'}
  style={exampleStyles.keyboardAvoidingView}
>
  <Toolbar editor={editor} />
</KeyboardAvoidingView>
```

**After (v1.0):**
```tsx
<KeyboardAvoidingView
  behavior={'padding'}
  style={exampleStyles.keyboardAvoidingView}
>
  <Toolbar editor={editor} />
</KeyboardAvoidingView>
```

The platform-specific check is no longer needed - use `'padding'` for both iOS and Android.

### SafeAreaView Import Changed

`SafeAreaView` now uses `react-native-safe-area-context` instead of `react-native`.

**Before (Pre-1.0):**
```tsx
import { SafeAreaView } from 'react-native';
```

**After (v1.0):**
```tsx
import { SafeAreaView } from 'react-native-safe-area-context';
```

Make sure you have `react-native-safe-area-context` installed and configured properly.

## Updated Dependencies

v1.0 is based on Tiptap v3, which brings improved performance and new features.

Update your dependencies:
```bash
yarn add @10play/tentap-editor@latest react-native-webview@latest
```

For iOS, update pods:
```bash
cd ios && pod install
```

## Need Help?

If you encounter issues during migration:

- Check the [examples](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/basic) for updated usage patterns
- Review the [API documentation](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/useEditorBridge) for current methods
- Open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/10play/10tap-editor/issues)

---

Source: https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/useEditorBridge

# useEditorBridge

a react hook that will return [EditorBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/EditorBridge)

The returned `editor` keeps the same reference for the lifetime of the component, so it is safe to use in dependency arrays. Pass that object to [RichText](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/Components#richtext). A spread copy such as `{ ...editor }` also works, but its option fields are a snapshot taken when it was made.

#### bridgeExtensions

`BridgeExtension[]`  
default: `TenTapStartKit`
A list of BridgeExtensions that will be added to the editor on the native side. Extensions with the same name are deduplicated and the last one wins, so spread `TenTapStartKit` first and put your configured bridges after it.

Bridges are read when the editor is created. Adding a bridge to the list after mount has no effect (a warning is logged in development); remount the editor instead.

#### initialContent

`string | object`  
default: `undefined`
initial content that will be loaded first on the editor. A string is parsed as HTML, an object as TipTap JSON.

#### parseOptions

`{ preserveWhitespace?: boolean | 'full'; from?: number; to?: number; topOpen?: boolean }`  
default: `undefined`
The serializable subset of ProseMirror [parse options](https://prosemirror.net/docs/ref/#model.ParseOptions) used when HTML is parsed: for `initialContent`, for [insertContent](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/EditorBridge#insertcontent) and for every [setContent](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/EditorBridge#setcontent) call that doesn't pass its own. It is read when the editor loads.

By default ProseMirror collapses runs of whitespace in HTML to a single space. Use `preserveWhitespace: 'full'` to keep them:

```tsx
const editor = useEditorBridge({
  initialContent: "<a href='hello'>hello</a>  <a href='world'>world</a>",
  parseOptions: { preserveWhitespace: 'full' },
});
```

With `'full'`, newlines and indentation between tags in pretty-printed HTML also become content. If you round-trip content saved from the editor, storing it with `getJSON()` keeps whitespace exactly with no parse options.

> **Note**
> `parseOptions` needs the 1.1 web editor. If you use a [custom editor bundle](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/setup/advancedSetup), rebuild it after upgrading.

#### autofocus

`boolean`  
default: `false`
when true the editor focuses at the end of its content when it becomes ready. It runs once per load, so it also refocuses after the WebView reloads.

#### avoidIosKeyboard

`boolean`  
default: `false`
This helps keep the cursor visible above the keyboard when the editor is full-screen and the virtual keyboard hides the bottom portion of the editor.

While the keyboard is up, `RichText` measures how far the keyboard and the views drawn on it (the [Toolbar](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/Components#toolbar), or your own toolbar marked with [useKeyboardAccessory](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/CustomKeyboardUtils#usekeyboardaccessory)) reach into the editor, and then:
- Adds that much bottom padding to the document, plus about one line
- Sets ProseMirror's scroll threshold and margin to the same value, so the line being typed stays about one line above the toolbar
- Scrolls the cursor back into view when the keyboard or toolbar moves over it
- Removes the padding when the keyboard is dismissed

This works the same for the system keyboard and an open custom keyboard, on iOS and Android, edge-to-edge or not, and wherever the editor ends: behind the keyboard, above a `KeyboardAvoidingView`, or inside one that already avoids the keyboard (where only the one-line margin is added). It is skipped when `dynamicHeight` is on, because the WebView is already only as tall as its content; see [useScrollToCaret](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/CustomKeyboardUtils#usescrolltocaret) for an editor that grows inside a `ScrollView`.

The measured inset applies to every editor, so an editor covered by the keyboard keeps its cursor visible even without this option. An editor that ends above the keyboard still keeps the line being typed about one line above its own bottom edge. If the editor reaches behind the keyboard and no view on the keyboard is marked, `RichText` assumes a toolbar of your own sits there and keeps the default toolbar height clear too; mark your toolbar with `useKeyboardAccessory` to measure it exactly. Until the first measurement, an editor with `avoidIosKeyboard` falls back to the 1.0 behaviour: the keyboard height on iOS (and wherever the keyboard overlays the window), or a fixed toolbar height on Android.

#### avoidKeyboard

`boolean`  
default: `false`
An alias of `avoidIosKeyboard` with a name that matches what it does. `avoidIosKeyboard` keeps working and wins when both are set.

#### scrollBottomOffset

`number`  
default: `0`
Extra space in px kept between the cursor and the bottom of the editor, on top of what `RichText` measures for the keyboard and toolbar. It is added to the scroll threshold and to the bottom padding, so new lines scroll into view before they reach something drawn over the editor that `RichText` cannot measure:

```tsx
const editor = useEditorBridge({
  scrollBottomOffset: 60, // e.g. the height of your floating action bar
});
```

The `Toolbar`, and views marked with [useKeyboardAccessory](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/CustomKeyboardUtils#usekeyboardaccessory), are already measured while the keyboard is up, so they need no offset.

Unlike calling [updateScrollThresholdAndMargin](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/EditorBridge#updatescrollthresholdandmargin) yourself, this value is kept when the keyboard opens and closes.

With `dynamicHeight` the padding is part of the content height, so the editor is that much taller than its text. A capped dynamic-height editor needs it to scroll its last line above something drawn over it (#308). Without it, a capped dynamic-height editor keeps about one line between the caret and its own bottom edge when it scrolls.

#### dynamicHeight

`boolean`  
default: `false`
when true the editor's webview keeps the same height as its content. It grows and shrinks with the content in any parent, not only inside a `ScrollView`.

- A height cap such as `maxHeight` on the container is respected. Once the cap is reached the editor scrolls internally and keeps its scroll position.
- Keyboard padding (`avoidIosKeyboard`) is not applied in this mode. When the editor grows inside a `ScrollView`, [useScrollToCaret](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/CustomKeyboardUtils#usescrolltocaret) scrolls the `ScrollView` to keep the line being typed above the keyboard.
- It can change after mount and the document is kept. A custom editor bundle built with a version before 1.1 keeps the value it loaded with and only the container height changes, as in 1.0. Rebuild the bundle to switch it at runtime.
- The content height in px is also sent as a `document-height` message. To read it yourself, pass `onMessage` to [RichText](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/Components#richtext) together with `exclusivelyUseCustomOnMessage={false}`.

To scroll a long document together with other content, put the editor inside your own `ScrollView`. See [Editor inside a ScrollView](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/scrollView).

#### disableColorHighlight

`boolean`  
default: `undefined`
when true the selection highlight will be off and when false will be on, on android this will be off by default, please see:
https://github.com/10play/10tap-editor/issues/184#issuecomment-2304826219

#### theme

`EditorTheme`  
default: `defaultEditorTheme` (light theme)
this prop can be used to customize default styles, see [theme example](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/customTheme)

#### editable

`boolean`  
default: `true`
When set to false the editor will be `readonly`. Changing it after mount calls `editor.setEditable`.

#### onChange

`() => void`  
A callback that is called each time the editor's content has changed. The content itself is not passed, so that every keystroke doesn't send the whole document from the WebView to React Native.

To keep the content in state, use [useEditorContent](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/useEditorContent), which is debounced and handles this for you:

```tsx
const editor = useEditorBridge({ initialContent });
const content = useEditorContent(editor, { type: 'html' });

useEffect(() => {
  if (content !== undefined) save(content);
}, [content]);
```

If you prefer `onChange`, fetch the content inside it with `editor.getHTML`, `editor.getJSON` or `editor.getText`, ideally debounced. The latest `onChange` is always the one called, so it can close over fresh state. See [Working with content](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/workingWithContent).

#### mergeStyles

`boolean`  
default: `false`
By default the `style` and `containerStyle` props of [RichText](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/Components#richtext) replace the editor's own styles (the default WebView styles and `theme.webview`, and `theme.webviewContainer`), as in 1.0. When `true`, your styles are merged on top of them instead. With `dynamicHeight` the content height is applied in both cases.

#### rpcTimeoutMs

`number`  
default: `undefined` (no timeout)
How long the async methods (`getHTML`, `getText`, `getJSON`, `getSelectedText`, and requests sent by custom bridges through `context.rpc`) wait for the WebView before rejecting with a `TentapRpcTimeoutError`. Without it they wait indefinitely, as in 1.0.

The time counts from the call, including any wait for the editor to load and time after the editor unmounted, so requests pending at unmount still reject. The option is read when the editor is created.

```tsx
import { TentapRpcTimeoutError } from '@10play/tentap-editor';

const editor = useEditorBridge({ rpcTimeoutMs: 5000 });

try {
  const html = await editor.getHTML();
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof TentapRpcTimeoutError) {
    // the WebView didn't answer in time
  }
}
```

#### customSource

`string`  
default: `SimpleEditorBundleString`
used in advance setup, an HTML string that will replace the default simple editor

#### webviewBaseURL

`string`  
default: `undefined`
The `baseUrl` of the WebView's HTML source. Relative URLs in your content and CSS (images, fonts) resolve against it. On iOS, point it at a `file://` directory to let the WebView read local files, for example [fonts loaded from a file](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/customCss#loading-fonts-from-a-file).

#### DEV

`boolean`  
default: `false`
prop used in advance setup, when true the webview will load DEV_SERVER_URL instead of the html string

#### DEV_SERVER_URL

`string`  
default: `http://localhost:3000`
prop used in advanced setup, a url string that points to the editor dev server

---

Source: https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/EditorBridge

# EditorBridge

An Interface of all the commands you can do with the editor on the react native side, can be extended with a [BridgeExtension](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions). With all of the bridges included in `TenTapStartKit` the EditorBridge will have the methods below.

A method only exists when its bridge is in `bridgeExtensions`. For example, `toggleBold` is added by `BoldBridge`; if you pass your own `bridgeExtensions` array without it, `toggleBold` is missing from both the object and its type.

Commands can be called right away, even before the editor has loaded. They are queued and sent in order once the editor is ready.

#### focus

`(pos?: 'start' | 'end' | 'all' | number | boolean | null) => void`
a function that will focus the editor and open the keyboard. If a [custom keyboard](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/CustomKeyboardUtils) is open, it closes and the system keyboard comes back.
extended by [CoreBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#coreextension)

#### blur

a function that will blur the editor and close the keyboard
extended by [CoreBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#coreextension)

#### webviewRef

`RefObject<WebView>`
a ref for the webview that renders the editor
extended by [CoreBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#coreextension)

#### getEditorState

`() => BridgeState`
a function that will return the most up to date BridgeState
extended by [CoreBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#coreextension)

#### getHTML

`() => Promise<string>`
an async function that will return the content of the editor in html format. List items are always wrapped in a paragraph (`<li><p>…</p></li>`); see [Rendering editor HTML](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/renderHtml) if you display the HTML outside the editor.
extended by [CoreBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#coreextension)

#### getText

`() => Promise<string>`
an async function that will return the content of the editor in text format
extended by [CoreBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#coreextension)

#### getJSON

`() => Promise<object>`
an async function that will return the content of the editor in json format
extended by [CoreBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#coreextension)

#### getSelectedText

`(range?: { from: number; to: number }) => Promise<string>`
an async function that returns the text of the current selection, read from the live editor inside the WebView. Pass a `range` to read another part of the document instead. Blocks are separated by `\n`, matching what the system "Copy" gives you.

```ts
const selected = await editor.getSelectedText();
const text = await editor.getSelectedText({ from: 1, to: 20 });
```

`from` and `to` are ProseMirror positions, the same numbers as [`BridgeState.selection`](./BridgeState.md#selection), not character offsets into `getText()`. Out of range values are clamped to the document.

Rejects with `TentapUnsupportedError` when the editor runs a custom bundle built with an older version; rebuild the bundle to use it.
extended by [CoreBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#coreextension)

#### setContent

`(content: Content, options?: { parseOptions?: ParseOptions; emitUpdate?: boolean }) => void`
a function that gets html as string or document object and sets it as the editor's content.

- `parseOptions` overrides the editor-level [parseOptions](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/useEditorBridge#parseoptions) for this call, e.g. `{ preserveWhitespace: 'full' }`.
- `emitUpdate` (default `true`) controls whether the change triggers `onChange` and [useEditorContent](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/useEditorContent).

extended by [CoreBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#coreextension)

#### insertContent

`(content: Content) => void`
inserts HTML, plain text or TipTap JSON at the cursor, replacing the current selection if there is one, and focuses the editor. HTML is parsed with the editor's [parseOptions](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/useEditorBridge#parseoptions). It works with the default editor, no custom bundle needed.

```ts
editor.insertContent('<strong>Hello</strong> world');
editor.insertContent('just some text');
```

The content still has to fit the editor's schema: a custom node type needs a bridge extension that defines it ([advanced setup](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/setup/advancedSetup)). A custom bundle built with an older version ignores the command; rebuild the bundle to use it.
extended by [CoreBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#coreextension)

#### setEditable

`(editable: boolean) => void`
a function that sets the editable state
extended by [CoreBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#coreextension)

#### setSelection

`(from: number, to: number) => void`
sets the selection of the editor
extended by [CoreBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#coreextension)

#### injectCSS

`(css: string, tag?: string) => void`
creates or updates the stylesheet with the given tag, see [Dynamically Updating CSS](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/customCss#dynamically-updating-css). The stylesheet is re-applied if the WebView reloads. For CSS that has to be there from the first paint, such as fonts, use `configureCSS` on a bridge instead.
default `tag`: `custom-css`
available on every editor, also without CoreBridge

#### injectJS

`(js: string) => void`
inject custom javascript into the editor's webview. Calls made before the editor is ready are queued.
extended by [CoreBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#coreextension)

#### updateScrollThresholdAndMargin

`(offset: number) => void`
a function that gets offset in px and changes [scrollThreshold](https://prosemirror.net/docs/ref/#view.EditorProps.scrollThreshold) [scrollMargin](https://prosemirror.net/docs/ref/#view.EditorProps.scrollMargin). `RichText` sets this itself when the keyboard opens or closes; to keep extra space permanently, use the [scrollBottomOffset](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/useEditorBridge#scrollbottomoffset) option.
extended by [CoreBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#coreextension)

#### toggleBold

`() => void`
will toggle bold on the editor if possible
extended by [BoldBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#boldbridge)

#### toggleItalic

`() => void`
will toggle italic on the editor if possible
extended by [ItalicBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#italicbridge)

#### toggleUnderline

`() => void`
will toggle underline on the editor if possible
extended by [UnderlineBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#underlinebridge)

#### toggleStrike

`() => void`
will toggle strikethrough on the editor if possible
extended by [StrikeBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#strikebridge)

#### toggleCode

`() => void`
will toggle inline code on the editor if possible
extended by [CodeBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#codebridge)

#### toggleBlockquote

`() => void`
will toggle blockquote on the editor if possible
extended by [BlockquoteBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#blockquotebridge)

#### toggleBulletList

`() => void`
will toggle bullet list on the editor if possible
extended by [BulletListBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#bulletlistbridge)

#### toggleOrderedList

`() => void`
will toggle order list on the editor if possible
extended by [OrderedListBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#orderedlistbridge)

#### toggleHeading

`(level: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6) => void`
gets level and toggles heading on the editor if possible
extended by [HeadingBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#headingbridge)

#### lift

`() => void`
will lift the list item on the editor if possible
extended by [ListItemBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#listitembridge)

#### sink

`() => void`
will sink the list item on the editor if possible
extended by [ListItemBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#listitembridge)

#### toggleTaskList

`() => void`
will toggle task list on the editor if possible
extended by [TaskListBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#tasklistbridge)

#### liftTaskListItem

`() => void`
will lift the task list item on the editor if possible
extended by [TaskListBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#tasklistbridge)

#### sinkTaskListItem

`() => void`
will sink the task list item on the editor if possible
extended by [TaskListBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#tasklistbridge)

#### undo

`() => void`
will undo the last history transaction if possible
extended by [HistoryBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#historybridge)

#### redo

`() => void`
will redo the last undo transaction if possible
extended by [HistoryBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#historybridge)

#### setColor

`(color: string) => void`
sets text color
extended by [ColorBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#colorbridge)

#### unsetColor

`() => void`
un-sets text color
extended by [ColorBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#colorbridge)

#### setHighlight

`(color: string) => void`
sets text highlight
extended by [HighlightBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#highlightbridge)

#### toggleHighlight

`(color: string) => void`
toggles text highlight
extended by [HighlightBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#highlightbridge)

#### unsetHighlight

`() => void`
un-sets text highlight
extended by [HighlightBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#highlightbridge)

#### setImage

`(src: string) => void`
gets image url string and inserts an image. If the image ends up as the last block of the document, an empty paragraph is added after it and the cursor moves there, so you can keep typing below it.
extended by [ImageBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#imagebridge)

#### setLink

`(link: string | null) => void`
gets link url as string and sets link. `''` removes the link and `null` does nothing. A URL without a scheme gets one added (`www.google.com` becomes `https://www.google.com`); see [LinkBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#linkbridge).
extended by [LinkBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#linkbridge)

#### setPlaceholder

`(newPlaceholder: string) => void`
will change the placeholder on run time
extended by [PlaceholderBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#placeholderbridge)

#### setHardBreak

`() => void`
inserts a line break (`<br>`) at the cursor
extended by [HardBreakBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#hardbreakbridge)

## Errors

The async methods can reject with these errors, both exported from `@10play/tentap-editor`:

| Error | When |
| --- | --- |
| `TentapRpcTimeoutError` | The WebView didn't answer within [rpcTimeoutMs](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/useEditorBridge#rpctimeoutms). Has `requestType` and `timeoutMs`. |
| `TentapUnsupportedError` | The editor bundle doesn't support the method, usually a custom bundle built with an older version. Has `capability`. |

---

Source: https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeState

# BridgeState

The BridgeState is the latest state of the editor webview on the native side, it's extendable by BridgeExtensions and is generally used with [useBridgeState](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeState#usebridgestate)

The list below is the interface of BridgeState in case you use `TenTapStarterkit` or using all the BridgeExtensions the lib exports, on each prop we specify what bridgeExtension adds it

### BridgeState properties

#### editable

`boolean`
Is the editor editable or not
extended by [CoreBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#coreextension)

#### empty

`boolean`
Is the editor empty or not
extended by [CoreBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#coreextension)

#### selection

`{ from: number; to: number }`
The selection on the editor-web. `from` and `to` are ProseMirror document positions, not character offsets: every block boundary adds a position, so they don't index into the string from `getText()`. To read the selected text use [getSelectedText](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/EditorBridge#getselectedtext).
extended by [CoreBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#coreextension)

#### isFocused

`boolean`
true when the editor is focused
extended by [CoreBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#coreextension)

#### isReady

`boolean`
true when the editor is fully loaded and can receive commands. It becomes true as soon as the web editor is created, whether or not it is editable or focused, and goes back to false while the WebView reloads (for example after the system kills its content process). You don't have to wait for it before calling editor methods: commands sent earlier are queued.
extended by [CoreBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#coreextension)

#### isBlockquoteActive

`boolean`
true when the cursor is where blockquote is active
extended by [BlockquoteBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#blockquotebridge)

#### canToggleBlockquote

`boolean`
true when it's possible to toggle blockquote
extended by [BlockquoteBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#blockquotebridge)

#### isCodeActive

`boolean`
true when the cursor is where code is active
extended by [CodeBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#codebridge)

#### canToggleCode

`boolean`
true when it's possible to toggle code
extended by [CodeBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#codebridge)

#### isBoldActive

`boolean`
true when the cursor is where bold is active
extended by [BoldBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#boldbridge)

#### canToggleBold

`boolean`
true when it's possible to toggle bold
extended by [BoldBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#boldbridge)

#### isItalicActive

`boolean`
true when the cursor is where italic is active
extended by [ItalicBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#italicbridge)

#### canToggleItalic

`boolean`
true when it's possible to toggle italic
extended by [ItalicBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#italicbridge)

#### isUnderlineActive

`boolean`
true when the cursor is where underline is active
extended by [UnderlineBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#underlinebridge)

#### canToggleUnderline

`boolean`
true when it's possible to toggle underline
extended by [UnderlineBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#underlinebridge)

#### isStrikeActive

`boolean`
true when the cursor is where Strike is active
extended by [StrikeBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#strikebridge)

#### canToggleStrike

`boolean`
true when it's possible to toggle Strike
extended by [StrikeBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#strikebridge)

#### isBulletListActive

`boolean`
true when the cursor is where bullet list is active
extended by [BulletListBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#bulletlistbridge)

#### canToggleBulletList

`boolean`
true when it's possible to toggle bullet list
extended by [BulletListBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#bulletlistbridge)

#### isOrderedListActive

`boolean`
true when the cursor is where ordered list is active
extended by [OrderedListBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#orderedlistbridge)

#### canToggleOrderedList

`boolean`
true when it's possible to toggle ordered list
extended by [OrderedListBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#orderedlistbridge)

#### isTaskListActive

`boolean`
true when the cursor is where task list is active
extended by [TaskListBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#tasklistbridge)

#### canToggleTaskList

`boolean`
true when it's possible to toggle task list
extended by [TaskListBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#tasklistbridge)

#### canLiftTaskListItem

`boolean`
true when it's possible to lift a task list item
extended by [TaskListBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#tasklistbridge)

#### canSinkTaskListItem

`boolean`
true when it's possible to sink a task list item
extended by [TaskListBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#tasklistbridge)

#### headingLevel

`number | undefined`
undefined when no heading is applied, number of the heading level
extended by [HeadingBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#headingbridge)

#### canToggleHeading

`boolean`
true when it's possible to toggle heading
extended by [HeadingBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#headingbridge)

#### canLift

`boolean`
true when it's possible to lift list item
extended by [ListItemBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#listitembridge)

#### canSink

`boolean`
true when it's possible to sink a list item
extended by [ListItemBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#listitembridge)

#### canUndo

`boolean`
true when it's possible to undo the doc history stack
extended by [HistoryBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#historybridge)

#### canRedo

`boolean`
true when it's possible to redo the doc history stack
extended by [HistoryBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#historybridge)

#### activeColor

`string | undefined`
undefined when no color is applied, string of the color that is active on the selection
extended by [ColorBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#colorbridge)

#### activeHighlight

`string | undefined`
undefined when no highlight is applied, string of the highlight that active on the selection
extended by [HighlightBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#highlightbridge)

#### isLinkActive

`boolean`
true when the link is in the selection
extended by [LinkBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#linkbridge)

#### canSetLink

`boolean`
true when it's possible to add link, for example when there is no selection it not possible
extended by [LinkBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#linkbridge)

#### activeLink

`string | undefined`
undefined when there is no link, string of the link that active on the selection position
extended by [LinkBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/BridgeExtensions#linkbridge)

### useBridgeState

a react hook to subscribe to changes on the BridgeState. It takes the `EditorBridge` and returns the latest `BridgeState`, re-rendering when it changes.

```tsx
const editorState = useBridgeState(editor);

<Button
  title={editorState.isBoldActive ? 'Unbold' : 'Bold'}
  onPress={() => editor.toggleBold()}
  disabled={!editorState.canToggleBold}
/>;
```

Before the editor is ready the core fields already have values (`isReady: false`, `isFocused: false`, `empty: true`, `selection: { from: 0, to: 0 }`, and `editable` from the option), so reading them never throws.

---

Source: https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/Components

# Components

## RichText

a components that wraps the webview that renders the editor

props:

| name                          | type           | default | description                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------- | -------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| editor                        | `EditorBridge` |         | The bridge instance that created with [useEditorBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/EditorBridge)                                                                                      |
| exclusivelyUseCustomOnMessage | `boolean`      | true    | When true, if you pass an `onMessage` prop (webview) this will override tentap's own `onMessage` property. You probably want to disable this, it's here for compatibility. |

`editor` must come from `useEditorBridge`; `RichText` throws an error for anything else. A spread copy such as `{ ...editor }` is still connected to the same WebView, but prefer passing `editor` itself.

you can also override any of the regular [WebView props](https://github.com/react-native-webview/react-native-webview/blob/HEAD/docs/Reference.md) although this is not recommended

### Passing your own onMessage

With the default `exclusivelyUseCustomOnMessage={true}`, passing `onMessage` turns off tentap's own message handling: the editor state, `dynamicHeight` and `onChange` stop updating. Pass `exclusivelyUseCustomOnMessage={false}` to receive every message while tentap keeps working:

```tsx
<RichText
  editor={editor}
  exclusivelyUseCustomOnMessage={false}
  onMessage={(event) => {
    const message = JSON.parse(event.nativeEvent.data);
    if (message.type === 'document-height') {
      console.log('content height', message.payload);
    }
  }}
/>
```

A warning is logged in development when `onMessage` is passed without `exclusivelyUseCustomOnMessage`. Messages may carry extra fields (such as `editorId`) besides `type` and `payload`; ignore the ones you don't use.

### Styles

- `style` replaces the editor's own WebView styles (including `theme.webview`), as in 1.0.
- `containerStyle` replaces `theme.webviewContainer`, as in 1.0.
- Set [mergeStyles](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/useEditorBridge#mergestyles) to merge both on top of the defaults instead.
- With `dynamicHeight`, the content height is always applied last, so a `flex: 1` or `height` in your styles doesn't override it. A `maxHeight` is respected.

### Editor swaps and reloads

Rendering a different `editor` in the same `RichText` mounts a new WebView for it. If the WebView's content process is killed by the system, `RichText` reloads it and restores the editor: queued commands, the last content set with `setContent` (or the last value read by [useEditorContent](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/useEditorContent)), injected CSS and settings such as `setEditable` and `setPlaceholder` are re-sent, and pending `getHTML`-style requests are retried. Edits made since that content was last read can be lost in this case.

## Toolbar

A react component of a basic Toolbar that include these features:

- Add link context
- Change headling context

- A lot of pre made toolbar items:
  - link
  - quote
  - code
  - bold
  - italic
  - checkList
  - underline
  - strikethrough
  - h1
  - h2
  - h3
  - h4
  - h5
  - h6
  - orderedList
  - bulletList
  - sync
  - lift
  - undo
  - redo

props:

| name   | type            | default               | description                                                             |
| ------ | --------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| editor | `EditorBridge`  |                       | The bridge instance that created with [useEditorBridge](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/EditorBridge) |
| hidden | `boolean`       |                       | a prop to control if toolbar shown. When not set, the toolbar is shown while the editor is focused and a keyboard (system or [custom](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/CustomKeyboardUtils)) is up. |
| items  | `ToolbarItem[]` | DEFAULT_TOOLBAR_ITEMS | array of ToolbarItem's that will be shown on the toolbar                |
| headingItems | `ToolbarItem[]` | HEADING_ITEMS | array of ToolbarItem's shown in the heading context (after pressing `Aa`) |
| shouldHideDisabledToolbarItems  | `boolean` | false | Indicates whether disabled items should be hidden. Applies to both `items` and `headingItems`. |
| ListComponent | `ComponentType<FlatListProps<ToolbarItem>>` | `FlatList` | The list that renders the main and heading toolbars, for example a `FlatList` from a bottom-sheet library. Not used on web. |

Each toolbar context (main, link, heading) renders its own list, so the heading toolbar always opens scrolled to the start.

### Customizing the heading toolbar

`HEADING_ITEMS` and `ToolbarContext` are exported, so you can build on the defaults. The first item of `HEADING_ITEMS` is the close button that goes back to the main toolbar:

```tsx
import { Toolbar, HEADING_ITEMS } from '@10play/tentap-editor';

<Toolbar editor={editor} headingItems={HEADING_ITEMS.slice(0, 4)} />; // close + H1-H3
```

If you write your own list, include an item that calls `setToolbarContext(ToolbarContext.Main)` so users can get back to the main toolbar.

### Link bar

Pressing the link item opens the link bar. The link is inserted with the **Insert** button or the keyboard's **Done** key, and the link bar stays open when the input loses focus. The input's placeholder (default `Type your URL here...`) is set with the `toolbar.linkBarTheme.hintText` key of the [theme](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/customTheme#link-bar).

> **Tip**
> If the editor or the toolbar is inside a `ScrollView`, `FlatList` or `KeyboardAwareScrollView`, set `keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"` on it. Otherwise the first tap on a toolbar button only dismisses the keyboard.

### ToolbarItem

The item rendered by the toolbar component

```ts
export interface ToolbarItem {
  onPress: ({ editor, editorState }: ArgsToolbarCB) => () => void;
  active: ({ editor, editorState }: ArgsToolbarCB) => boolean;
  disabled: ({ editor, editorState }: ArgsToolbarCB) => boolean;
  image: ({ editor, editorState }: ArgsToolbarCB) => any;
  // Accessibility label, read by screen readers and UI test tools
  label?: string;
}

type ArgsToolbarCB = {
  editor: EditorBridge;
  editorState: BridgeState;
  setToolbarContext: (
    context: ToolbarContext | ((prev: ToolbarContext) => ToolbarContext)
  ) => void;
  toolbarContext: ToolbarContext;
};
```

See how we add a custom toolbar item in the [color keyboard example](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/examples/colorKeyboard)

## Custom keyboard components

`CustomKeyboard`, `ColorKeyboard` and `EditorKeyboardAvoidingView` are documented in [Custom Keyboard Utils](https://10play.github.io/10tap-editor/docs/api/CustomKeyboardUtils).
